name: Dolutegravir
route_note: oral tablet once daily (twice daily with some resistance or interacting drugs); dispersible tablets for children
originator: Shionogi and ViiV Healthcare (Shionogi–ViiV joint venture)
owner: ViiV Healthcare (GSK, Pfizer, Shionogi); generics in low- and middle-income countries

discovery.note: Second-generation INSTI with a high genetic barrier to resistance.

tagline: High-barrier integrase inhibitor at the heart of the WHO-preferred TLD regimen
summary: Dolutegravir is a second-generation integrase strand transfer inhibitor taken once daily, with potent activity and a high barrier to resistance. Combined with tenofovir and lamivudine as the generic TLD tablet, it became WHO's preferred first-line HIV treatment and is taken by many millions of people. A 2018 neural tube defect signal was later found to be much smaller than first feared.
mechanism: HIV integrase inserts the reverse-transcribed viral DNA into the host genome. Dolutegravir binds the integrase–viral DNA complex (intasome) and chelates the two magnesium ions in the active site, blocking the strand transfer step.

Its long dissociation half-life from the integrase–DNA complex contributes to its high barrier to resistance; emergent resistance in first-line use is rare, though mutations such as R263K, G118R and Q148 pathways can reduce susceptibility.
uses: HIV-1 infection in adults and children (from 4 weeks and 3 kg in some labels) in combination with other antiretrovirals
Two-drug regimens with lamivudine (Dovato) or rilpivirine (Juluca)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Tivicay is approved in August 2013; EU approval follows in 2014.

history.title: Generic TLD
history.detail: Licensing through the Medicines Patent Pool and pricing deals allow generic tenofovir/lamivudine/dolutegravir (TLD) at under $75 per year in many countries.

history.title: Neural tube defect signal
history.detail: The Tsepamo study in Botswana reports a possible excess of neural tube defects with conception on dolutegravir; regulators issue warnings.

history.title: WHO preferred
history.detail: With more data showing a much smaller risk, WHO recommends dolutegravir as preferred first- and second-line therapy for all populations, including women of child-bearing potential.

history.title: Paediatric dispersible
history.detail: Dispersible 10 mg dolutegravir tablets for young children are approved in the US, and soon after in low-income countries.

pk.bioavailability: not established; taken with or without food

serious: hepatotoxicity, particularly with hepatitis B or C co-infection
possible small increase in neural tube defects with periconception exposure

facts: Dolutegravir slightly raises serum creatinine by inhibiting the renal transporter OCT2, without affecting true glomerular filtration.
It must be separated in time from antacids and supplements containing polyvalent cations, which bind it.
By the early 2020s more than 20 million people were receiving dolutegravir-based treatment, mostly as generic TLD.

references.title: Zash R et al. Neural-tube defects with dolutegravir treatment from the time of conception. NEJM 2018
